reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) describes a slow cooling rate used to avoid delamination in a different material system, which does not support any of the key premises about heat transfer, hysteresis reduction, or magnetocaloric improvement in FeMnNiGeSi films.
premises: A high thermal conductivity interlayer between substrate and film accelerates heat extraction during magnetic cooling cycles.
Accelerated heat extraction reduces thermal lag and inhomogeneous temperature fields in the film.
Reduced thermal lag leads to narrower magnetic hysteresis loops.
Narrower hysteresis loops correspond to improved magnetocaloric response (efficiency, entropy change).
Improved thermal management permits faster cycle frequencies.
